### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to establish that the marketplace-search problem is an information bottleneck, not a reasoning deficit. Paper [1] discusses the information bottleneck principle in representation learning but does not address marketplace search or agentic systems. Paper [3] revisits LLM reasoning via the information bottleneck but focuses on reasoning capabilities rather than marketplace search. Paper [5] provides a theoretical justification for the information bottleneck in deep learning but does not address marketplace search or agentic systems. Paper [19] identifies efficiency limits in agentic systems but does not establish the marketplace-search problem as an information bottleneck. None of the prior papers substantively establish the same empirical relationship between marketplace search and information bottlenecks.

### Mechanism
The contribution tests agent-side interventions (prompting to extract fit signals, inference scaling) against truncated 40-token descriptions on a restaurant marketplace. Paper [17] proposes a probabilistic framework for inference-time scaling but does not apply it to marketplace search or truncated descriptions. Paper [13] discusses agentic AI for consumer-to-consumer marketplaces but does not test agent-side interventions against truncated descriptions. Paper [19] studies agentic systems efficiency but does not test interventions like prompting or inference scaling. None of the prior papers use the same mechanism.

### Evaluation
The evaluation design involves measuring welfare outcomes (e.g., prompting drops welfare from 68.51 to -35.85; 4.7x more inference compute gives -29.71) to show agents cannot recover lost fit signals through reasoning. Paper [19] conducts empirical studies on agentic systems efficiency but does not use welfare metrics or the same evaluation design. Paper [13] evaluates agentic AI in consumer-to-consumer marketplaces but does not use welfare outcomes as a metric. Paper [17] evaluates inference-time scaling but does not measure welfare outcomes. None of the prior papers use the same evaluation design.

### Domain
The contribution operates in the domain of agentic marketplace search/agentic commerce. Paper [13] addresses consumer-to-consumer marketplaces, which fall under the broader domain of agentic commerce. Paper [14] proposes a multi-agent framework for e-commerce search, which also falls under the domain of agentic commerce. Paper [19] studies agentic systems efficiency, which includes agentic commerce. The domain is covered by prior work.
